name: Güneş
presentingProblem: Sometimes I lose hours and I don't know where they went. It's like I am watching my life from behind glass, and I came here because I am tired of pretending I remember things I don't.
backstory: Güneş is a first-generation university graduate from a small Anatolian town, now working as a junior accountant in Ankara. Growing up, her emotional needs were rarely acknowledged at home, and her family explains her current episodes as a matter of nerves or spiritual unease rather than something to take to a psychiatrist. She has built a quiet life around routines that hide the gaps in her memory from colleagues and friends. Coming to therapy feels like a betrayal of her family's view of what is wrong with her. She is articulate about ideas but uncertain about her own continuity as a person.

coreBeliefs: I don't know who I really am
Parts of me are not mine
If I look too closely at myself, there is nothing there
intermediateBeliefs: If people knew about the gaps, they would think I am unwell
Staying on the surface is safer than asking deeper questions
I have to manage this quietly, otherwise my family will worry in the wrong way
automaticThoughts: Wait, what was I just saying?
This room doesn't feel real today
I think I agreed to something this week, I'm not sure what
That memory belongs to someone else
I was going to say something important — never mind
triggers: Being asked to recall specific recent events in order
Long silences that draw attention inward
Discussions of identity or who she 'really' is
defenses: Derealization described in soft, uncertain language
values: Education and earning her own place in the world
Being seen as steady and reliable at work
Understanding what is actually happening to her, even if it is hard
